title: Metering: add request_outcome + retry_reason dimensions (with cardinality guards)
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Internal-only: metering events and billing aggregates now include request_outcome + retry_reason dimensions (guarded) to support reconciliation and dispute triage.
description: Summary This PR adds two low-cardinality dimensions to hosted API metering events and downstream aggregation: request_outcome and retry_reason. This unblocks reconciliation work where retries/transport errors are currently indistinguishable from successful billed usage, and supports billing dispute investigations where customers see “extra tokens” that are actually retry attempts. The dimensions are added end-to-end (event emission -> streaming ingestion -> warehouse tables -> billing-ready aggregates) with explicit cardinality safeguards and dashboards/alerts compatibility notes. Context / Motivation Finance + Support cases (e.g., SUP-3112) and meter sanity checks identified that a subset of endpoint failures and client-side retries could inflate raw token counts in intermediate telemetry views, even when the final invoice logic correctly excludes some categories. The lack of explicit outcome/retry attributes makes reconciliation noisy and forces manual log spelunking. ENG-4823 calls for a clear separation of billed vs non-billed usage at the event level, without blowing up cardinality or breaking existing rollups. Changes (high-level) 1) Event schema additions Added properties to the metering event schema (metering.v2): request_outcome: enum success | client_cancelled | client_error | server_error | rate_limited | auth_failed | timeout | unknown retry_reason: enum none | client_retry | upstream_retry | network_retry | gateway_retry | unknown Notes: request_outcome is computed at the gateway/billing hooks boundary where we already have HTTP status, streaming termination reason, and internal error codes. retry_reason is best-effort. If we can’t determine a reason, we emit unknown (NOT raw error strings). 2) Cardinality safeguards Implemented an allowlist-based mapper for retry_reason and request_outcome. Any unmapped value collapses to unknown. Added a hard check in the aggregation job that fails the run if distinct values exceed thresholds for these dimensions (defensive guard to prevent accidental high-cardinality strings). Thresholds: request_outcome distinct <= 20/day; retry_reason distinct <= 50/day (per env). Added metrics: metering.dimensions.distinct_count{dimension=request_outcome|retry_reason} metering.dimensions.unknown_rate{dimension=...} 3) Downstream aggregation + billing exports Propagated both fields into: raw_events table (partitioned) billing_usage_facts (hourly rollup) invoice_aggregates (daily, billing-ready) Also included in the billing export schema for auditability, but behind a feature flag (billing_export_include_outcome_dims) so Finance can validate in staging before we expand the export footprint in prod. 4) Query + documentation updates Updated example reconciliation queries to filter billed usage as request_outcome=success AND retry_reason in (none, upstream_retry) (subject to billing policy; this PR does NOT change billing policy). Added a short note to the metering data contract doc explaining semantics and the non-goal (not a canonical retry taxonomy; just enough for consistent slicing). 5) Backfill plan This PR does not backfill historical data. Once merged, we can start capturing dimensions immediately. Backfill (if needed for audit window) should be coordinated with Finance/SRE due to replay load and alert suppression; tracked separately under ENG-4826. Files/Areas changed (representative) services/gateway/src/metering/outcome_mapper.ts services/gateway/src/metering/emit_metering_event.ts proto/metering/v2/metering_event.proto pipelines/metering/aggregation/hourly_rollup.sql pipelines/metering/aggregation/guards/distinct_dimension_guard.ts billing/export/schema/billing_export.avsc (flagged) docs/data-contracts/metering-v2.md Tests Added unit tests for outcome mapping from (status_code, disconnect_reason, error_code) -> request_outcome Added property-based tests to ensure unknown collapse for unrecognized retry reasons Added aggregation guard tests verifying distinct-count failure behavior CI / Verification - ✅ unit (gateway) - ✅ unit (pipelines) - ✅ integration: metering pipeline staging replay (24h sample) - ✅ lint/typecheck - ✅ warehouse query snapshots updated (expected new columns) Manual verification notes Ran a staging replay of 2026-02-03 traffic with the new dimensions enabled; distinct counts observed: request_outcome=8, retry_reason=6, unknown_rate ~0.4% (mostly legacy clients with missing retry headers). Confirmed invoice_aggregates totals are unchanged when grouping without the new dims (i.e., backward-compatible rollups). Follow-ups / Open questions - Define the canonical billing-side rule for whether certain retry reasons are billable under specific contract language (Legal/Finance; not in scope here). - If we decide to include these fields in customer-facing usage exports, we should review wording and reduce confusion (“client_cancelled” vs “disconnect”). - Hook up the distinct-count guard metric to the meter anomaly dashboards (ENG-4824); this PR only emits the metrics. Reviewer notes / discussion Logan Wright (Telemetry) Requested changes: Can we guarantee we never emit raw error strings? Also please add a guard on unknown_rate so we notice if mapping breaks. Nadia Rahman (Author) Reply: Outcome/retry are enums only; the mapping layer explicitly drops raw codes. Added metrics for unknown_rate and a warning log when unknown_rate > 5% in a 15m window (non-paging). Cole Summers (Billing hooks) Comment: Where does retry_reason come from? We don’t currently have a stable retry header for all SDKs. Nadia Rahman Reply: For now, we infer from gateway retry middleware vs upstream retries (e.g., 502 from model router) and from the internal “attempt” counter when present. If absent, retry_reason=unknown. This still lets us isolate obvious gateway retries from successful usage. Emily Stone (Finance) Comment: Please confirm this doesn’t change invoice totals and that Finance can slice billed vs non-billed for reconciliation. Nadia Rahman Reply: No billing logic changes. Totals unchanged unless you explicitly filter/group by new dims. The point is to make deltas explainable; Finance can now exclude client_cancelled/server_error when validating raw telemetry vs billing-ready aggregates. Allison Grant (SRE/Obs) Comment: The distinct-value guard failing a run could page SRE during backfills; can we make it configurable by environment? Nadia Rahman Reply: Yes—thresholds are per env, and the guard is WARN-only in dev. In prod/staging it fails the aggregation job but does not page; we emit an alertable metric and link to runbook (to be added in ENG-4824). Approvals - ✅ Logan Wright - ✅ Cole Summers - ✅ Emily Stone - ✅ Allison Grant Merge Notes Squashed and merged. Deployment will roll out with the next gateway deploy train. Enablement: once deployed, update reconciliation queries and dispute triage templates to reference request_outcome and retry_reason where relevant.
